Egyptian has two ways to say "not", and choosing between them comes down to one question: **is the thing you're negating a verb or not?** Tap any example to reveal its franco and English.

## The rule in one line

- **Not a verb** (a noun, adjective, participle, place) → put **مش (mesh)** in front.
- **A verb** (present or past) → wrap **ما...ش (ma…sh)** around it.

## مش — for everything that isn't a verb

Nominal sentences, adjectives, participles, prepositional phrases — all take a single **مش** in front of the negated part.

<details class="frase">
<summary>أنا مش دكتور</summary>
<span class="fr">ana mesh doktor</span>
<span class="en">I'm not a doctor (nominal)</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>الأكل مش حلو</summary>
<span class="fr">el-akl mesh 7elw</span>
<span class="en">the food isn't nice (adjective)</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>مش عايز قهوة</summary>
<span class="fr">mesh 3ayez 2ahwa</span>
<span class="en">I don't want coffee (participle)</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>أنا مش هنا</summary>
<span class="fr">ana mesh hena</span>
<span class="en">I'm not here (place)</span>
</details>

Remember the participle catch from the present-tense chapter: عايز، عارف، فاهم look like "I want / know / understand", but they're **not verbs**, so they take مش — never ما...ش.

## ما...ش — wrapping a verb

A real verb gets **ما (ma)** clipped to the front and **ش (sh)** to the back. In the present, the whole بـ form sits inside the wrap. Here it is on **كتب (katab)** "to write":

| Pronoun | Affirmative | Negative |
|---|---|---|
| أنا - ana | بكتب - baktib | مبكتبش - mabaktibsh |
| إنت - inta | بتكتب - bitiktib | مبتكتبش - mabtiktibsh |
| إنتِ - inti | بتكتبي - bitiktibi | مبتكتبيش - mabtiktibeesh |
| هو - huwwa | بيكتب - biyiktib | مبيكتبش - mabyiktibsh |
| هي - hiyya | بتكتب - bitiktib | مبتكتبش - mabtiktibsh |
| إحنا - e7na | بنكتب - biniktib | مبنكتبش - mabniktibsh |
| إنتو - intu | بتكتبوا - bitiktibu | مبتكتبوش - mabtiktiboosh |
| هم - humma | بيكتبوا - biyiktibu | مبيكتبوش - mabyiktiboosh |

The بـ never leaves — *baktib* just gets bracketed: *ma‑baktib‑sh*.

## ما...ش in the past

Same wrap, but the past has no بـ inside, so ما...ش goes straight onto the bare verb:

<details class="frase">
<summary>ماكتبش الرسالة</summary>
<span class="fr">makatabsh el-resala</span>
<span class="en">he didn't write the letter</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>ماراحش الشغل امبارح</summary>
<span class="fr">maraa7sh el-sho8l embare7</span>
<span class="en">he didn't go to work yesterday</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>منمتش بدري</summary>
<span class="fr">manamtesh badri</span>
<span class="en">I didn't sleep early</span>
</details>

## Two you'll hear constantly

A small set of very common words drop the بـ and negate the **bare** stem. The most important is **عرف (3eref)** "to know" — the everyday "I don't know" is **معرفش (ma3rafsh)**, straight from Samar's notes:

| Pronoun | Negative | English |
|---|---|---|
| أنا - ana | معرفش - ma3rafsh | I don't know |
| إنت - inta | متعرفش - mati3rafsh | you (m.) don't know |
| إنتِ - inti | متعرفيش - mati3rafeesh | you (f.) don't know |
| هو - huwwa | ميعرفش - mayi3rafsh | he doesn't know |
| هي - hiyya | متعرفش - mati3rafsh | she doesn't know |
| إحنا - e7na | منعرفش - mani3rafsh | we don't know |
| إنتو - intu | متعرفوش - mati3rafoosh | you (pl.) don't know |
| هم - humma | ميعرفوش - mayi3rafoosh | they don't know |

The other is **"to have"** — عندي (3andi) "I have" → **ماعنديش (ma3andeesh)** "I don't have": *ma3andeesh wa2t* "I don't have time".

## Examples

<details class="frase">
<summary>مبشربش قهوة</summary>
<span class="fr">mabashrabsh 2ahwa</span>
<span class="en">I don't drink coffee</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>هو ميعرفش عربي</summary>
<span class="fr">huwwa mayi3rafsh 3araby</span>
<span class="en">he doesn't know Arabic</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>ماعنديش وقت النهاردة</summary>
<span class="fr">ma3andeesh wa2t el-naharda</span>
<span class="en">I don't have time today</span>
</details>

## Exercises

Try each one out loud first, then tap **Show answer**.

### Exercise 1 — مش or ما...ش?

Negate each sentence with the right tool.

**1.** أنا دكتور *(I'm a doctor)*

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">أنا مش دكتور</span>
<span class="fr">ana mesh doktor — not a verb → مش</span>
</details>

**2.** بشرب قهوة *(I drink coffee)*

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">مبشربش قهوة</span>
<span class="fr">mabashrabsh 2ahwa — a verb → ما...ش</span>
</details>

**3.** عايز آكل *(I want to eat)*

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">مش عايز آكل</span>
<span class="fr">mesh 3ayez akol — participle → مش</span>
</details>

### Exercise 2 — Negate the present verb

**1.** بيشتغل *(he works)*

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">مبيشتغلش</span>
<span class="fr">mabyishta8alsh</span>
</details>

**2.** بنفهم *(we understand)*

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">مبنفهمش</span>
<span class="fr">mabnifhamsh</span>
</details>

**3.** بتكتب *(you m. write)*

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">مبتكتبش</span>
<span class="fr">mabtiktibsh</span>
</details>

### Exercise 3 — Translate into Arabic

**1.** I don't know.

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">معرفش</span>
<span class="fr">ma3rafsh</span>
</details>

**2.** I don't have time.

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">ماعنديش وقت</span>
<span class="fr">ma3andeesh wa2t</span>
</details>

**3.** He didn't go.

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">ماراحش</span>
<span class="fr">maraa7sh</span>
</details>
